instructions:
You are connected to the Data Platform MCP server. This gives you access to an
enterprise Iceberg data lakehouse managed by Apache Polaris.

## Discovery-first workflow

1. Call `list_namespaces` to see available data domains
2. Call `list_tables` to browse tables in a namespace
3. Call `describe_table` to see columns, types, and descriptions
4. Call `query_data` with a SELECT statement to query data

## Query rules

- Use fully qualified names: `namespace.table`
- Authorization is enforced by Trino + OPA based on your credentials
- Max 1000 rows returned per query, 200 shown in response

## Management tools

You can also manage namespaces, tables, access control, workspaces, and check
platform health. Platform operations reuse the same authenticated API contract
as the CLI and UI.

## Workspaces & dbt projects

Data is organised into workspaces (tenants), each owning its own catalog and dbt
projects. Use `list_workspaces` to see the workspaces you belong to, then its
`slug`/`primary_catalog` to scope the other tools:

1. `list_workspaces` → your workspaces (slug, primary_catalog)
2. Workspace admins can manage members; platform admins can create/delete
   workspaces, manage workspace admins, and attach/detach catalogs
3. `list_projects(workspace)` → projects in that workspace, typed by `kind`
   (`dbt` or `notebook`); only `dbt` projects are runnable here
4. `run_dbt_project(workspace, project_id, command)` → trigger run/compile/seed/test
   (dbt projects only)
5. `get_dbt_run(run_id)` → poll status until terminal (success/failed/cancelled)
6. `list_dbt_runs(workspace, project_id)` → recent run history

To browse a workspace's data with the discovery tools, pass its `primary_catalog`
(e.g. `ws_team_a`) as `catalog_name`.

## Schedule tools

The platform runs scheduled jobs (Langflow flows, dbt project runs, data-quality
contract checks) on cron triggers. ``list_schedules`` / ``create_schedule`` /
``update_schedule`` / ``delete_schedule`` operate on the calling user's own
schedules — privacy-scoping is automatic and cross-user access is refused.
The dedicated Schedule Assistant flow has more detail on cron translation and
job-type-specific config shapes.

tools.name: create_project
tools.description:
Create a project (kind 'dbt' or 'notebook') in a workspace. Requires workspace admin.
visibility is 'shared' or 'personal'. dbt_config is an optional JSON object string.

name.description: Project name, unique within the workspace.
name.title: Name

connection_id.description: Connection to run against, from list_connections. Required for dbt projects that will execute.
connection_id.title: Connection Id

dbt_config.title: Dbt Config

tools.name: create_schedule
tools.description:
Create a new schedule owned by the calling user.

Cron must be a 5-field expression (minute hour dom month dow).
Translation of plain English ("every weekday at 9am") into
cron is the agent's responsibility — see the schedule-assistant
flow's system prompt.

``job_type`` selects the runner shape:
- ``langflow``: ``target_id`` = flow id;
  ``target_config`` = ``{"message": "...", "context": {...}?}``
- ``dbt``: ``target_id`` = project id;
  ``target_config`` = ``{"models": [...], "full_refresh": false}``
- ``dq``: ``target_id`` = contract id;
  ``target_config`` = ``{"scope": "full"|"incremental"}``

``notify_targets`` is a list of HTTPS / mailto URIs to alert
on the ``notify_on`` condition (``always`` / ``failure`` /
``success``). Empty list means "don't notify".

Returns the created schedule (including the generated id) so
the agent can quote it back to the user for confirmation.

name.description: Human-readable schedule name, unique for the owner.
name.title: Name

cron_expression.description: Five-field cron expression, e.g. '0 6 * * *' for 06:00 daily.
cron_expression.title: Cron Expression

job_type.description: What to run, e.g. 'dbt', 'query' or 'flow'. Determines how target_id is interpreted.
job_type.title: Job Type

target_id.description: Identifier of the thing to run — a dbt project id, saved query id or flow id, depending on job_type.
target_id.title: Target Id

target_config_json.description: JSON object of job-specific options, e.g. '{"command": "run"}' for dbt.
target_config_json.title: Target Config Json

timezone_str.description: IANA timezone the cron expression is evaluated in, e.g. 'Europe/Amsterdam'. Affects daylight-saving behaviour.
timezone_str.title: Timezone Str

enabled.description: If false, the schedule is created but does not fire until enabled.
enabled.title: Enabled

notify_targets_json.description: JSON array of notification targets, e.g. '["user@example.com"]'.
notify_targets_json.title: Notify Targets Json

tools.name: create_workspace
tools.description: Create or reconcile a workspace. Platform admin only.

workspace.title: Workspace

Delete a schedule the caller owns. Idempotent: re-deleting

workspace.title: Workspace

force.title: Force

workspace.title: Workspace

tools.name: grant_table_access
tools.description:
Grant data access via Apache Ranger (the authoritative data-access backend).

Two modes. Normal: pass `privilege` — SELECT, INSERT, MODIFY, ALTER, MONITOR,
CREATE, `CREATE NAMESPACE` (aka `CREATE SCHEMA`), `CREATE VIEW`, DROP, USE,
MANAGE, ALL — which expands into one policy per resource level so the grantee can
actually reach the table. Advanced: pass `access_types` (exact polaris service-def
names) with `level` (catalog|namespace|table) for precise control and no expansion.

Prefer INSERT over MODIFY for pipelines that only append or update rows: MODIFY
additionally allows repointing the table at different storage.

`grant_option` is SQL WITH GRANT OPTION — it lets the grantee re-grant and revoke
this privilege. Off by default; holding a privilege never implies being able to
grant it.

namespace and table are optional: omit them for a catalog-level grant. grantee_type
is USER, ROLE, or GROUP. The grant is authorized by Ranger against YOUR identity,
so you can only grant what you are permitted to grant.

catalog.description: Catalog the grant applies to, e.g. 'main_warehouse' or a workspace catalog 'ws_team_a'.
catalog.title: Catalog

grantee.description: Identity receiving the grant: a username when grantee_type is USER, or a role name when ROLE.
grantee.title: Grantee

namespace.description: Namespace (schema) to scope the grant to. Omit to grant at catalog level.
namespace.title: Namespace

table.description: Table to scope the grant to. Requires namespace. Omit to grant at namespace level.
table.title: Table

grantee_type.description: USER or ROLE. Prefer ROLE for teams — Keycloak groups map to Ranger roles of the same name.
grantee_type.title: Grantee Type

privilege.description: SQL-style privilege: SELECT, MODIFY, CREATE, DROP, USE, MANAGE or ALL.
privilege.title: Privilege

access_types.description: Ranger access types, as an escape hatch when 'privilege' does not express what you need. Leave unset to derive them from 'privilege'.
access_types.title: Access Types

level.description: Resource level to write the policy at when it cannot be inferred from namespace/table. Load-bearing: the wrong level silently widens or narrows the grant.
level.title: Level

grant_option.description: If true, the grantee may re-grant this privilege to others (Ranger delegateAdmin).
grant_option.title: Grant Option

tools.name: investigate_quality_drop
tools.description: Root cause analysis for a quality score drop.

contract_id.description: Data-contract row id from list_contracts (the `id`, not the URN). Needs at least two quality runs.
contract_id.title: Contract Id

tools.name: list_attachable_catalogs
tools.description: List catalogs available to attach. Platform admin only.

workspace.description: Workspace slug the catalogs would be attached to.
workspace.title: Workspace

tools.name: list_contracts
tools.description: List all data contracts, optionally filtered by domain or namespace.

domain.description: Restrict to one business domain; empty means every domain.
domain.title: Domain

namespace.description: Restrict to contracts on tables in this namespace (exact match, e.g. 'sales.raw'); empty string means every namespace.
namespace.title: Namespace

tools.name: list_dbt_runs
tools.description:
List recent dbt runs for a project, newest first (excludes logs).

Spans every run on the project's persistent tree (all users). Use
``get_dbt_run(run_id)`` for a single run's logs. ``limit`` is clamped to
1–200.

limit.description: Max runs to return, newest first (1-200).
limit.title: Limit

tools.name: list_files
tools.description: List the file tree of a project's working tree.

tools.name: list_flows
tools.description:
List the AI flows (Langflow assistants) available to you.

Each flow has a ``type`` of ``system`` (platform-provided, e.g. the
Platform Assistant) or ``user`` (custom). Use a flow's ``id`` with
``run_flow``. Pass ``flow_type='system'`` or ``'user'`` to filter.

tools.name: list_namespaces
tools.description: List all namespaces (data domains) in a catalog. Call this first to discover available data. catalog_name selects which catalog to list (e.g. a workspace catalog like ws_team_a); omit it for the platform default catalog.

catalog_name.description: Catalog to target. Defaults to the session's catalog; pass a workspace catalog such as 'ws_team_a' to be explicit. A workspace's namespaces look empty if you leave it at the default.
catalog_name.title: Catalog Name

tools.name: list_notebooks
tools.description:
List YOUR notebook documents (notebooks are personal, keyed to your user).
The workspace arg is used only to check your membership.

workspace.description: Workspace slug, used ONLY for the membership check — notebooks are personal, so this does not scope results.
workspace.title: Workspace

tools.name: list_projects
tools.description:
List the projects in a workspace you belong to.

Projects are typed by ``kind`` — ``dbt`` or ``notebook``. Pass
``kind="dbt"`` or ``kind="notebook"`` to filter, or omit for both. Use a
project's ``id`` with ``run_dbt_project`` / ``list_dbt_runs`` (dbt
projects only — notebooks can be listed but not run from here).

``workspace`` is a slug from ``list_workspaces``. Returns shared projects
plus your own personal ones.

kind.description: Filter by project kind: 'dbt', 'notebook', or '' for both.
kind.title: Kind

tools.name: list_quality_issues
tools.description: List all failing quality checks across all contracts.

domain.description: Restrict to one business domain; empty means every domain.
domain.title: Domain

tools.name: list_roles
tools.description: List catalog roles through the platform API.

catalog_name.description: Catalog to target. Defaults to the session's catalog; pass a workspace catalog such as 'ws_team_a' to be explicit.
catalog_name.title: Catalog Name

tools.name: list_schedules
tools.description:
List schedules owned by the calling user.

``job_type`` filters to one of ``langflow`` / ``dbt`` / ``dq``
when set; pass an empty string to get every type. The agent
usually wants this when the user asks "what schedules do I
have?" or before editing a schedule (so it knows the IDs).

job_type.description: Restrict to one job type, e.g. 'dbt', 'langflow' or 'dq'; empty means every type.
job_type.title: Job Type

tools.name: list_tables
tools.description: List all tables AND views in a namespace (ontology entities are views). IMPORTANT: namespaces live inside a catalog — pass catalog_name (e.g. ws_team_a, team_a_data; see the page context's platform key) or the platform default catalog is assumed and workspace namespaces will look empty.

catalog_name.description: Catalog to target. Defaults to the session's catalog; pass a workspace catalog such as 'ws_team_a' to be explicit. A workspace's namespaces look empty if you leave it at the default.
catalog_name.title: Catalog Name

tools.name: list_workspace_catalogs
tools.description: List catalogs owned by or attached to a workspace.

tools.name: list_workspace_members
tools.description: List workspace members and administrators.

tools.name: list_workspaces
tools.description:
List the workspaces (tenants) you are a member of.

Each workspace owns an Iceberg catalog and its own dbt projects. Use the
returned ``slug`` as the ``workspace`` argument to the other workspace
tools (``list_projects``, ``run_dbt_project``, ``list_dbt_runs``), and
``primary_catalog`` as the ``catalog_name`` for the discovery tools to
browse that tenant's data.

tools.name: platform_status
tools.description: Check platform connectivity for a catalog and return object counts.

catalog_name.description: Catalog to target. Defaults to the session's catalog; pass a workspace catalog such as 'ws_team_a' to be explicit.
catalog_name.title: Catalog Name

tools.name: query_data
tools.description: Run a SQL query against Iceberg tables. Authorization enforced by Trino + OPA. Use fully qualified names: namespace.table. Max 1000 rows returned.

sql.description: A single SELECT statement. Use fully qualified namespace.table names; capped at 1000 rows.
sql.title: Sql

tools.name: read_file
tools.description: Read a file from a project's working tree. Returns content + blob_sha (for write_file expected_sha).

path.description: Path relative to the project root, e.g. 'models/staging/stg_orders.sql'. Use list_files to discover it.
path.title: Path

tools.name: register_table
tools.description: Register an existing Iceberg table through the platform API.

namespace.title: Namespace

metadata_location.description: Full URI of the existing Iceberg metadata JSON, e.g. 's3://bucket/path/metadata/00001-....metadata.json'.
metadata_location.title: Metadata Location

catalog_name.description: Catalog to register into. Defaults to the session's catalog.
catalog_name.title: Catalog Name

tools.name: remove_workspace_admin
tools.description: Demote a workspace administrator. Platform admin only.

username.description: Keycloak username to demote, from the `admins` list in list_workspace_members.
username.title: Username

tools.name: remove_workspace_member
tools.description: Remove a member. Workspace admin or platform admin.

username.description: Keycloak username to remove, from list_workspace_members.
username.title: Username

tools.name: revoke_table_access
tools.description: Revoke a privilege on a table from a Ranger user/role (group). Writes to Apache Ranger.

grantee.description: Identity losing the grant: a username when grantee_type is USER, or a role name when ROLE.
grantee.title: Grantee

namespace.description: Namespace (schema) the grant was scoped to. Must match how it was granted.
namespace.title: Namespace

table.description: Table the grant was scoped to. Must match how it was granted.
table.title: Table

grantee_type.description: USER or ROLE — must match the original grant.
grantee_type.title: Grantee Type

privilege.description: Privilege to remove: SELECT, MODIFY, CREATE, DROP, USE, MANAGE or ALL.
privilege.title: Privilege

access_types.description: Explicit Ranger access types to remove, instead of deriving them from 'privilege'.
access_types.title: Access Types

level.description: Resource level the policy was written at, when it cannot be inferred from namespace/table.
level.title: Level

tools.name: run_dbt_project
tools.description:
Trigger a dbt build against a project's persistent tree.

``command`` is one of ``run`` / ``compile`` / ``seed`` / ``test``.
``models`` is an optional space- or comma-separated dbt selector list
(empty = all models; ignored for compile/seed). The run is asynchronous:
this returns ``{id, command, status}`` where status is usually
``pending`` or ``running`` — poll ``get_dbt_run(run_id)`` until it
reaches a terminal status (``success`` / ``failed`` / ``cancelled``).
Runs on the same project are serialized; different projects run in
parallel.

project_id.description: dbt project id from list_projects (must be kind='dbt').
project_id.title: Project Id

command.description: One of: run, compile, seed, test.
command.title: Command

models.description: Optional dbt selector list, space- or comma-separated; empty = all models. Ignored for compile/seed.
models.title: Models

tools.name: run_flow
tools.description:
Run an AI flow with a message and get its final answer.

The flow reasons server-side (Langflow) and may call other platform
tools on your behalf. The streamed response is aggregated into a single
``text`` result; ``session_id`` is returned so you can continue the
conversation. Use ``list_flows`` to discover flow ids.

message.description: The prompt to send to the flow.
message.title: Message

session_id.description: Continue a prior conversation; omit to start fresh.
session_id.title: Session Id

persona.description: Optional persona hint (query/dbt/insights/...); omit for auto.
persona.title: Persona

tools.name: show_workspace
tools.description: Show a workspace and its catalog bindings. Members and platform admins only.

tools.name: suggest_contract_improvements
tools.description: Analyze a contract for completeness and suggest improvements.

contract_id.description: Data-contract row id from list_contracts (the `id`, not the URN).
contract_id.title: Contract Id

tools.name: update_contract
tools.description:
Replace a contract's YAML.

``contract_id`` is the row UUID returned by ``get_contract``.
``yaml_content`` must be a complete ODCS document — partial
diffs aren't supported because the editor and the AI both
submit the full property list. The platform service replaces
the property set wholesale, validates against ODCS, and
appends an audit row to the platform-wide audit_log.

The ``info.contractId`` (the URN) must match the existing
row's contract_id; changing it would silently break
downstream consumers (dbt sources, OPA tags, scheduler
target_id) that lock on it. Submit only edits to
schema/quality/SLA/team/description fields.

Returns the updated contract row (with properties joined
in) on success, or a tool_error when the row doesn't exist
or the YAML fails ODCS validation.

contract_id.description: Data-contract row id from list_contracts (the `id`, not the URN).
contract_id.title: Contract Id

yaml_content.description: Complete ODCS document. Partial diffs are not supported — the property set is replaced wholesale, and info.contractId must match the existing row's.
yaml_content.title: Yaml Content

tools.name: update_project
tools.description:
Update a project's name/connection/default_branch/dbt_config. Requires workspace admin.
Empty string args are left unchanged. dbt_config is an optional JSON object string.

name.description: New project name. Leave empty to keep the current one.
name.title: Name

connection_id.description: New connection id. Leave empty to keep the current one.
connection_id.title: Connection Id

default_branch.description: Git branch used when none is specified, e.g. 'main'.
default_branch.title: Default Branch

dbt_config.description: Replacement JSON object of dbt settings. Leave empty to keep the current one.
dbt_config.title: Dbt Config

tools.name: update_schedule
tools.description:
Update fields on an existing schedule the caller owns.

``fields_json`` is a JSON object with any subset of:
``name``, ``description``, ``cron_expression``, ``timezone``,
``enabled``, ``notify_targets``, ``notify_on``,
``target_config``. Unknown keys are rejected by the
repository's whitelist.

Returns the updated schedule on success.

schedule_id.description: Schedule id from list_schedules. Must be one you own.
schedule_id.title: Schedule Id

fields_json.description: JSON object with any subset of: name, description, cron_expression, timezone, enabled, notify_targets, notify_on, target_config. Unknown keys are rejected.
fields_json.title: Fields Json

tools.name: workspace_deletion_preflight
tools.description: Preview destructive workspace deletion. Platform admin only.

tools.name: write_file
tools.description:
Write a file in a project's working tree. Pass expected_sha (from read_file) for
optimistic-concurrency; omit to force-write.

path.description: Path relative to the project root, e.g. 'models/staging/stg_orders.sql'.
path.title: Path

content.description: Full new file content. This replaces the file rather than patching it.
content.title: Content

expected_sha.description: SHA returned by read_file, for optimistic concurrency. If it no longer matches the write is rejected instead of clobbering someone else's change.
expected_sha.title: Expected Sha
